skill.name: proposal-pdf
skill.description: Guides the creation of small-business proposal PDFs with verified facts, clear pricing, client branding, HTML layouts, and page-by-page quality checks.
skill.summary: Create client proposal PDFs with verified pricing, restrained sales copy, and visual checks.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around CSS, a browser API example, and a filename template. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or data exfiltration in SKILL.md. The documented workflow uses PDF rendering tools and requires explicit permission before sending proposals to clients.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit inline CSS and HTML examples in Markdown. They do not execute Ruby or shell commands.
The backticks format a Playwright page.pdf example for legitimate PDF rendering. No shell execution or untrusted command interpolation appears in this instruction.
The backticks format the filename template Proposal <Business>.pdf in Markdown. The text is a naming guideline, not executable shell syntax.

content.value_statement: Client proposals can lose credibility through incorrect prices, unclear scope, or poor formatting. This skill guides verified content, branded layouts, PDF rendering, and page-by-page review.
actual_capabilities: Build a source-backed fact list for client details, service scope, prices, extras, and third-party costs.
Organize proposals into cover, benefits, included services, investment, and next-step pages.
Guide concise copy without guaranteed results, invented discounts, or unsupported deadlines.
Apply client-focused branding, including a typographic wordmark when no client logo exists.
Guide HTML print layouts and PDF rendering through Playwright, Chromium, or an available PDF skill.
Require page PNG inspection, extracted-text comparisons, and a delivery report listing verification gaps.
limitations: This is a written workflow, not a bundled PDF generator or executable template.
PDF rendering, PNG export, and text extraction require tools available in the host environment.
Prices, client facts, assets, and payment terms must come from supplied or verifiable sources.
Visual review and fact checks do not guarantee sales results or replace human approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Agency Service Proposal
use_cases.description: Turn a client brief and confirmed price list into a branded proposal with clear scope, extras, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Present a Website or Design Quote
use_cases.description: Create a concise proposal using the client name as a wordmark when no suitable logo exists.

use_cases.title: Explain Monthly Advertising Costs
use_cases.description: Separate management fees from advertising spend and explain campaign handling if the service pauses.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a proposal for [client] using [brief] and [price list]. Use verified facts only. Ask about missing prices before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare proposal content from supplied sources.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Branded PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a five-page proposal PDF from [approved copy] and [assets]. Use a wordmark if needed. Keep the agency logo secondary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: format approved content for a client without a usable logo.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Monthly Service Offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an advertising proposal from [service terms]. Separate management fees, free extras, and ad spend. Explain pauses using confirmed terms. Avoid guaranteed outcomes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: present recurring costs and service conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Verify the Delivery Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Render [approved proposal] to PDF and page PNGs using available tools. Compare extracted text with [fact sources]. Report paths and unchecked items. Do not send.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: complete rendering, visual inspection, and source verification.

output_examples.input: An approved website proposal with verified client details and pricing, but no client logo.
output: Cover: Proposal for Greenway Studio, with a client wordmark and a smaller agency logo.
Included services: the approved website scope, listed in short steps.
Investment: the confirmed price and approved payment terms.
Next step: the agreed start process, without unsupported deadlines.

output_examples.input: A completed monthly advertising proposal and its approved fact list, ready for final review.
output: Delivery report: proposal PDF path and page preview paths.
Fact checks: client name, contact details, management fee, and advertising budget compared with approved sources.
Visual checks: page previews reviewed for clipped text, overlap, empty pages, and logo clarity.
Verification gaps: unavailable checks are listed explicitly; client delivery remains pending authorization.

best_practices: Supply authoritative client details, approved pricing, service terms, and image sources before drafting.
Confirm rendering and extraction tools are available before planning PDF and PNG deliverables.
Review every page preview and verify extracted facts before approving client delivery.
anti_patterns: Inventing prices, discounts, payment terms, deadlines, or service inclusions.
Promising sales results, search rankings, or click counts that the service cannot guarantee.
Sending the proposal directly to the client without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions for researching, writing, designing, rendering, and checking small-business proposal PDFs.

faq.question: Does it include a PDF generator?
faq.answer: No. It guides available tools such as Playwright or Chromium, or an existing PDF skill.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the client brief, verified business details, approved service scope, pricing, payment terms, and available brand assets.

faq.question: Can it work without a client logo?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends displaying the client name as a typographic wordmark instead of inventing a logo.

faq.question: How are facts and layout checked?
faq.answer: The workflow compares extracted PDF text with source facts and requires inspection of every page PNG.

faq.question: Will it send the proposal to my client?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit sending without explicit authorization. They direct the agent to hand deliverables to the relationship owner.
